title: State v. Abdifatah Abdulkadir Yusuf, No. A25-2003, nonprecedential opinion

acquisition.channel: Official Minnesota Judicial Branch PDF host

supports: October 26 nonprecedential opinion in A25-2003 reversed the district court's post-verdict acquittal and remanded for reinstatement of six jury guilty verdicts on aiding and abetting theft by swindle.
The district court had previously acquitted on a separate racketeering count before the six other counts went to the jury; the appeal's disposition does not reinstate that count.

The court described trial testimony and documentary evidence concerning billing by Promise Health Service LLC, including a lead investigator's testimony that fraudulent payments exceeded $7.2 million; this is not a restitution or recovery order.
The appellate disposition is a procedural reversal/remand, not a newly entered prison sentence.
does_not_support: An entered post-remand sentencing judgment, updated restitution or actual collections.
That a conviction was entered on the previously dismissed racketeering charge.
Attributing alleged conduct by other named provider organizations to them solely due to shared space or associations.
locators: Opinion pp. 9–11, allegations and procedural history
notes: Preserve the distinction between a jury verdict, intervening post-verdict acquittal, appellate reversal, and later reinstatement on remand. Confirm the district court's entry and any further appellate activity before claiming final sentencing.
